We have list of templates. Need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The template_id likely is reaction_id? The description says template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). In search result each entry has reaction_id and template_hash. Probably template_id is reaction_id. So choose a template that matches our target molecule's amide formation. The molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. Contains an amide: C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring. The retrosynthetic step would break amide to carboxylic acid and amine. The template should be amide formation. Among results, which template corresponds to amide formation? Look at retro_smarts_template: first entry: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'. This seems to be amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine with an activated ester? Might be appropriate.

Second entry: retro_smarts_template '[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]>>O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]'. That's amide formation from acid? Actually forward: O-... to amide.

Third entry similar.

We need to ensure template matches our molecule. Could test with check_smiles_reaction_template_matching for each template_id. Let's try first template reaction_id 401931.
We'll call check_smiles_reaction_template_matching.
